_note: ENTRY SURFACES vs DISPATCHER ROLE — the decoupling that lets a user control where they access the system from without breaking the single-dispatcher invariant. An ENTRY SURFACE is where a person TYPES a request (any host they like). The DISPATCHER ROLE (assigns seats, runs the risk gate) is ONE config-bound provider. A non-dispatcher surface classifies + drafts a brief and hands it to the dispatcher; it never self-assigns other seats or implements outside its own seat. To move the whole system to a different entry habit — or to a user who has no Codex — edit `dispatcher.provider` and the `can_dispatch` flags here; policy prose does not change.

dispatcher.rule: Exactly one dispatcher holds the queue/assign/risk-gate at a time. If the dispatcher provider is down, the owner at the console may hand a COMPLETE brief straight to the implementer for non-gate work; gate work parks. A phone surface never implements.

codex-cli.note: The default dispatcher surface. Full dispatch: classify, stamp review, brief, assign, gate, refill.

claude-code.note: Show status (usage-status), classify + stamp + draft a brief, then hand to the dispatcher. Never assign other seats or implement outside the Claude review/judgment seat. This machine's /orchestrate runs in this mode.

cursor.note: IDE surface. Draft-and-hand like Claude Code. Never re-home dispatch onto the IDE.

phone.note: Read status, forward briefs/reports, approve owner gates. Never implements or dispatches.

rules.non_dispatcher_hosts: classify + stamp + draft brief, then hand to the dispatcher; never self-assign other seats or implement outside the surface's own seat
rules.entry_is_free: Any surface may be the place a request starts. Where a request is TYPED is the user's choice; who ASSIGNS seats is config-bound.
rules.portability: A user without Codex sets dispatcher.provider to a capable provider they own (e.g. opus-4.8) and marks that surface can_dispatch:true. The single-dispatcher invariant is unchanged; only the holder moves. See subscriptions.json portability_examples and USER-GUIDE.md §Entry points.
